# fah-core-metal

> A Folding@home core that runs real FAH work units on Apple Silicon GPUs through OpenMM's Metal platform. Runs on Apple Silicon Macs (M-series GPUs) through Metal. Tested on the M3 Ultra and the M2.

minicore is a Folding@home core that runs FAH's OpenMM work units on the GPU of Apple Silicon Macs through Metal. Tested on the M3 Ultra and the M2, it folds a real FAH unit, project 18264 with 919,221 atoms, and matches FAH's core 0x27 on every check FAH doesn't control. On P18264 the M3 Ultra takes 0.87 times the time core 0x27 takes on an RTX 5060 Ti, measured on one unit, one Mac and one card.

fah-core-metal is not affiliated with or endorsed by Folding@home. It never connects to FAH servers. Its results carry no FAH signature.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal#readme): figures for speed, trajectories, accuracy and parity with core 0x27, where it differs, how to build and run it, FAQ
- [Evidence](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal/blob/main/docs/EVIDENCE.md): the run and raw record behind every number in the README, and the README's longer text: what was tested, how it matches core 0x27, the test unit's transcript
- [Design notes](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal/blob/main/docs/design-notes.md): how the README and the core are laid out, and why

## Source

- [src/](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal/tree/main/src): minicore, the core
- [build.sh](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal/blob/main/build.sh): fetches OpenMM with the Metal platform, builds it as static libraries and links the core
- [docs/data/](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal/tree/main/docs/data): the CSVs behind every figure
